## Guard threat model: constructed-input findings are accepted (2026-10-22, docs/sdlc/specs/direct-mode-diet.md)

> The guards defend against an agent's mistakes — a careless `rm`, a write to
> a frozen policy during a task, a commit with a secret — not against an agent
> that constructs a command to exhaust them. A command built to time the guard
> out is visible in the transcript and in the journal, and the human gate at
> T4+ is the boundary for anything that matters. Findings that need such a
> command are accepted here and do not open a task.

This covers, below: the `sh -c`/`eval` residual of "The path guard is quadratic
on long lines", the remaining spellings of "`sh -c` spellings `segments_of`
does not read", "`shell_segments` is quadratic on one long segment", "One
amplifying symlink keeps `realpath -m` past the hook timeout", "`realpath`'s
line count can balance while its lines are misaligned", "Batched movers cost a
few µs more per segment, near the clock" and "The token pass strips quotes one
character at a time". Entries already fixed are not touched. What happens when
a guard runs past the runtime's 10 s hook timeout (`settings.common.json:45`)
is the runtime's rule, not the guard's; this acceptance does not claim the
guard fails closed. The same threat model is in `.ai/policies/safety.md`.

label: RISK
likelihood: deliberate padding, or a very long generated command; the deny side of every path rule is lost for that call.
status_why: fixed (T-2026-10-15-004) except the `sh -c`/`eval` re-segmentation, whose residual is accepted (2026-10-22, docs/sdlc/specs/direct-mode-diet.md) — see "Padded `sh -c` segments still outrun the path guard" below. Causes, profiled: (1) `[[ =~ ]]` (glibc regexec, unanchored search restarting at every offset) on a long line; (2) a fork-heavy pass per token and per mover operand; (3) found during the fix: in a UTF-8 locale GNU grep re-verifies a line its DFA accepts with the same regexec (a 200 KB line that *matches* took > 20 s; in C, 12 ms), and bash's `${s%$'\n'}`, `${w#*=}` and `${w##*/}` cost 0.7 s, 9.5 s and 4.5 s on 140–200 KB. Observation, not fixed: the "directory that holds runtime configuration" deny prints `task ?` instead of the task id, because `covers_protected` runs in `$( )` and `task_in_flight`'s `AI_TASK_ID` is lost with the subshell; the characterization golden pins it.

## Shared tree (T-2026-10-13-004): accepted risks (a)–(v)

The shared policies, agent contracts, workflows and templates moved to
`<home>/claude-agentic/ai/` (project copy = override). Plan rev 2 accepts the
following; each is open unless marked.

- **(a) Guard Bash write detection misses `rm`/`mv`/`cp` destinations on frozen paths.** `hooks/ai-path-guard.sh:273-337` matches copiers and readers by their source arguments; a destination on a task-protected path (now including `<home>/claude-agentic/ai/`) is not recognised. Worse for the shared tree: the protection pattern `(^|/)\.(claude|codex)/claude-agentic/(ai/|ai-path$)` (`hooks/ai-path-guard-defaults.json:54`) needs a path *inside* `ai/`, so `rm -rf …/claude-agentic/ai`, `mv <dir> …/claude-agentic/ai` or `cp -r <dir>/ai …/claude-agentic/` replace the whole tree unmatched even once destinations are classified (security review). Suggested fix: classify the last argument of `cp`/`mv`/`install` as a write target, and widen the pattern to `ai(/|$)` with a negative test on the bare directory, in one hooks task. Status: fixed (T-2026-10-15-001) — a destination pass before the fast path classifies the last operand (or `-t DIR`) of `cp`/`mv`/`install`/`rsync`, `dest/basename(source)` for every source and every `mv` source; `rm`/`rmdir`/`unlink` arguments count as writes; the pattern is `ai(/|$)` and the pre-filter turns an inner `$` into a token boundary (`tests/fixtures/path-guard/51-56`, the shared-tree loop in `tests/test-ai-path-guard.sh`). Residuals, from the STRONG review (`.ai/reports/T-2026-10-15-001/review-report.md`), all confirmed against the new guard and none fixed here: (1) parent directories of every directory-shaped pattern are not matched — `rm -rf ~/.claude/claude-agentic/`, `rm -rf .claude/hooks`, `rm -rf .ai/state/`, `mv .claude /tmp/x`, `cp -r src/agents .claude/`, `rsync -a /tmp/evil/ .claude/`, and `mv x .ai/policies` over the bare project directory; (2) a verb not at the start of a `|;&`/newline segment is not seen — `for f in …; do cp "$f" .claude/agents/; done`, `if …; then cp …`, `(cp …)`, `$(cp …)`, `FOO=1 cp …`, `time cp …`, `{ rm -rf …; }`, backslash-newline continuations; (3) prose false denies — a `;`, a newline or a heredoc body that starts with `rm`/`cp`/`mv` naming a protected path is treated as a command (`echo "step 2; rm -f .ai/state/current.json"`, a commit message, a heredoc writing a test script), the same class as the existing `writers` rule; (4) `-t` glued to other short flags (`cp -rt DIR src`) or attached (`-tDIR`) reads the value as a source; (5) rsync — a remote path still matches the unanchored pattern, and an option with a separate value at the end (`--exclude X`, `-e ssh`) becomes the destination; (6) the redirect-stripping sed eats a digit glued to a redirect (`y2>/dev/null` → `y`), harmless with the current patterns; (7) `WHY_TASK` still says "policies and workflows" — rewording it re-records every WHY_TASK golden entry; (8) on HEAD too: `ln -sf /tmp/evil.md .claude/agents/x.md` is allowed (`writers` checks ln's first argument only), and unnormalised paths (`$SH/./ai`, `$SH//ai`, `cd $SH && rm -rf ai`) skip the pre-filter. Suggested fix for (1)–(3): quote- and heredoc-aware segmentation with `do|then|(|{|time|VAR=` as segment heads, and a reverse prefix test that denies removing or overwriting any directory above a protected or task path — its own hooks task. (1)–(3) status: fixed (T-2026-10-15-002) — `shell_segments` (`hooks/ai-path-guard.sh`, one awk pass) splits a command into simple commands, quote-, heredoc- and comment-aware, strips `if/then/do/!/{/time/exec/command/nohup/env/sudo`, their flags and `NAME=value` heads, and re-reads the string of `sh|bash|… -c` and `eval` once; the verb rules (`movers`, `writers`, `removers`, `modes`, `ddwrite`, `inplace`) match those segments; the destination pass covers `rm`/`rmdir`/`unlink` too and denies any `rm` operand, `mv` source, `dest/basename(src)` or (for an rsync/cp source ending in `/`) the destination itself that lies above a protected file, or above a frozen runtime file while a task is in flight (`covers_protected`: lexical first, then the `.ai`/`.claude`/`.codex`/home roots under it at depth 3, then the path at depth 6, ≤20000 entries); dependency files do not count, `~`/`$HOME`/`${HOME}` are expanded and paths go through `realpath -m` (`tests/fixtures/path-guard/57-85`, the "parent directories and segmentation" section of `tests/test-ai-path-guard.sh`). Residuals: an unquoted heredoc body's `$(…)` runs in the shell but is data to the guard's model; `readers`, `copiers`, the `>` redirect rule, the `ln` rule and the one-liner tripwire still match the raw line, so prose that reads or redirects a protected path is still denied (err on the deny side); `rm -rf <scratch fixture holding .ai/state/*.json>` is denied, consistent with the per-file rule; `sudo -u USER cmd` keeps USER as the verb; `xargs rm`, `find -exec rm` and a path built from a variable other than `HOME` are not modelled; a glob is never expanded (`rm -rf .claude/*`, `rm -rf .ai/*`), `cp -T` onto a frozen directory is not a contents copy to the guard, and `cd .ai && rm -rf state` resolves against the session cwd — all three allowed on the previous guard too. The STRONG review's three regressions (a here-string or an arithmetic `<<` read as a heredoc, hiding the lines after it; `sh -c` re-read only as the segment's verb, and `$'…'` not unquoted) were fixed in remediation R1 and are pinned in the same test section.
- **(b) `.ai/agents/` is not task-protected and is now an override path.** `hooks/ai-path-guard-defaults.json:46` freezes `.ai/(policies|workflows|templates)/` only; an agent could drop `.ai/agents/reviewer.md` during a task and shadow the shared contract. Suggested fix: add `agents` to that pattern (guard data, its own task). Status: fixed (T-2026-10-15-001) — `agents` is in the pattern; Write in a task is denied, Read and no-task Write stay allowed. Observation for a human: `.ai/policies/security.md:66-68` still says the frozen set is `.ai/policies/` and `.ai/workflows/`; it is a project policy, frozen in-task, and should name `agents/` and `templates/` too.
- **(c) The installed tree is guarded only while a task is in flight and only in `.ai/` projects.** Parity with the installed agents and skills (M7). `ai-path --tree-hash` fingerprints the tree, and a real install prints `backup: claude-agentic/ai -> …` when the installed tree differed (it then restores it); `install.sh --dry-run` does **not** show a changed tree — it prints only the static file count. Status: accepted.
- **(d) Deny and comment text name files that became shared.** `hooks/ai-git-guard.sh:109` says `.ai/policies/release.md`; `skills/project-init/templates/project-config.toml:14` says `.ai/policies/tooling.md`. Both are frozen in this task and both files are reached through the router. Suggested fix: reword to `policies/release.md` / `policies/tooling.md` in a hooks task. Status: fixed (T-2026-10-15-001) — both reworded; the 35 characterization entries that embed `WHY_DEPLOY` were re-recorded.
- **(e) Gemini/Junie-only machines have no shared tree.** `install.sh` installs it only for Claude Code and Codex homes; `safety.md` and `security.md` stay project-owned (Q5=A), all 29 shared files (none of which is `safety.md` or `security.md`) are unreachable for those runtimes once 0006 deletes the copies. Status: accepted.
- **(f) This repository's own `.ai/` overrides shadow what it ships.** Its `.ai/policies|agents|workflows|templates` are edited copies; until a human runs 0006 here and resolves each override, sessions in this repo read the local versions, not `ai/`. Status: open, post-close human step.
- **(g) "treat `.ai/policies/` as binding" now covers only the 7 project-owned policies.** `instructions/stub.md:24` and `:37` (frozen). The router's `## Shared files` section carries the rule for the shared ones. Status: open (L6).
- **(h) Edited overrides get no upstream changes, and "behind" cannot be detected.** The history keeps only hashes of shared files (Q1=A), so there is no merge base; `/project-update` repeats an override hint on every run instead (M6). Status: accepted.
- **(i) Homes absent on this machine are unchecked.** `require_shared` (`skills/project-update/update.py`, `MigrationContext.require_shared`) checks every installed declared home; a teammate whose home lacks the tree is protected only by the old plugin's exit 2 on schema 6 (M2). Status: accepted.
- **(j) The no-commit rollback restores deletions only.** Without a commit of `.ai/`, the originals under `.ai/reports/project-update-<date>/original/` bring back the deleted copies, nothing else: `.ai/VERSION` stays 6 until a human writes `5` into it (README and `skills/project-update/SKILL.md` say so), and the router keeps its section. Git (`git restore --source=<commit before the migration> --staged --worktree -- .ai`) is the primary rollback; `update.py` hints when `.ai/` is dirty (M4). Status: accepted.
- **(k) Two-rename install window.** `install_shared` (`install.sh:565-588`) moves the old tree aside and the new one in; between the two `mv` calls there is no `ai/`. A reader in that instant fails and retries. Status: accepted (L3).
- **(l) Plain `--check` says "matches" while a `[shared] delete?` waits.** Same behaviour as for rules; only `--apply` lists it. Status: open.
- **(m) `/ai-init` told the agent to fill "Project specifics" in shared policies.** `skills/ai-init/SKILL.md` asked for project specifics in `database.md`, `tooling.md` and `release.md` (unconditionally for `tooling.md`); with no override, the resolver points at `<home>/claude-agentic/ai/`, unprotected outside a task, so one project's specifics would land in the policy every project reads. Status: fixed in the review remediation (R1): `/ai-init` now writes them only into a deliberate full-copy override under `.ai/policies/` and never into the shared tree. Residual: those three shared files still carry an empty `## Project specifics` placeholder, and `ai/policies/tooling.md:42` itself says "List what this project actually enables … under **Project specifics** below" — an agent reading the shared policy outside `/ai-init` is told to write into the shared file. Suggested fix: reword the shared text to name the project override (a change to `ai/`, its own task).
- **(n) The symlink check runs at plan time only.** `unsafe_target` (`skills/project-update/update.py`) is not repeated in `apply` before `os.remove`; a parent directory swapped for a symlink between plan and delete is followed (same process, same bytes required, needs write access to `.ai/`). Suggested fix: re-run `unsafe_target` just before `keep_original`/`os.remove`. Status: open.
- **(o) Environment and home detection.** `CLAUDE_AGENTIC_SHARED` is honoured outside tests (`scripts/ai-path`, `update.py`) and silently redirects every shared read; `require_shared` then checks only that tree. `require_shared` reads the Codex home from `CODEX_HOME` and ignores `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, while `install.sh` installs to `CLAUDE_DIR`/`CODEX_DIR`; a custom install location is also outside the guard pattern. Suggested fix: gate the variable behind `CLAUDE_AGENTIC_TEST=1`, and resolve homes the way `install.sh` does. Status: open.
- **(p) `ai-path` edge cases.** It takes the nearest `.ai/` above the working directory, so a nested `.ai/` created during a task (a plain `mkdir` is not detected) redirects resolution; `--root /nonexistent` exits 0 with the shared path; `os.path.isfile` follows a symlinked override that points outside the project. Status: open.
- **(q) `install_shared` keeps one backup only** (`install.sh`): a later install overwrites the previous backup of a customised tree. Status: accepted.
- **(r) Markdown is never scope-checked by the step diff.** `skills/ai-task/sensors.py:513-515` skips files in `unbudgeted_scopes` (docs) before the allowed-files check, so Step 9's README/docs change measured "0 files"; and `ai/**` scores as `docs`/T0, so a change to shipped policy text in this repository is neither re-scored nor scope-checked. Suggested fix: add `ai/**` to a pipeline scope and run the allowed-files check before the unbudgeted early exit. Status: open.
- **(s) `put_section` places the section before the first matching heading line** (`skills/project-update/update.py`, `put_section`), also one inside a fenced code block or a duplicated heading; the result passes the one-section guard silently. Needs a human edit that duplicates the follow heading. Status: open.
- **(t) A router section at the very end without a final newline** glues onto the next heading when the merge moves it (`put_section`). 0006 always writes the newline; needs a human to strip it. Status: open.
- **(u) One CRLF line makes `router_merge` rewrite the whole router in CRLF** (`crlf = b"\r\n" in ours`). Status: open.
- **(v) The template's `## Shared files` text never reaches a router that already has the section.** By design of `router_merge`; a future migration that changes the shared set must rewrite the section itself. Status: accepted.

## Legacy managed-block markers (T-2026-10-14-001)

- **(a) `render_instructions.block_of` and `adopt.py` know only the current marker.** `block_of` (`skills/project-update/render_instructions.py`) and the AGENTS.md reader in `adopt.py` look for `<!-- claude-agentic:start -->` alone, so an instruction file with a legacy `Codex-agentic` pair measures as "no block" and the dry run hints `AGENTS.md (split?) — run /project-update --adopt` until `--apply` has renamed the markers. `update.py` (`find_block`) is the one place fixed in this task; the same lookup in the other two is left as is. Status: fixed in T-2026-10-14-002 — the lookup lives in `render_instructions.find_block` (str and bytes); `block_of`, `update.find_block` and `adopt.Candidate` all use it. Residual: a second legacy pair in the same file, or a pair whose two markers differ in case, is still left in place.
- **(b) `install.sh` still doubles a legacy pair.** The Codex path (`install.sh:607-628`) and `block_size` (`install.sh:160`) look for the current markers only, so an AGENTS.md with a `Codex-agentic` pair gets a second block appended at install or reinstall; the next `/project-update` then renames the legacy pair and leaves two current blocks. Found by the T-2026-10-14-001 review. Status: fixed in T-2026-10-14-002 — `managed_block` renames a legacy pair before the in-place update and says so; `block_size` measures either pair.
- **(c) `skills/ai-init/scaffold-ai.sh:103` greps the current marker only.** `/ai-init` on a file with a legacy `Codex-agentic` pair appends a second block — the doubling this task fixes in `update.py`, `adopt.py` and `install.sh`. Found by the T-2026-10-14-002 review; outside its seven files. Suggested fix: the same either-pair test as `install.sh` `managed_block`. Status: fixed in T-2026-10-14-003 — the scaffold tests for either spelling of the start marker and appends nothing beside a legacy pair; the file is left as it is for `/project-update` to rename (`tests/test-scaffold-idempotency.sh`).
- **(d) `update.py:1110-1116` budget hint on a pristine legacy block.** `block_of` now returns a legacy block, and the over-budget hint compares it verbatim with the shipped bytes, so it says "edited here, the plugin will not rewrite it" although `--apply` renames and rewrites it. Only when the block exceeds the budget; the hint text only. Suggested fix: compare through `current_markers`. Status: not reproducible (T-2026-10-14-003) — `budget_hints` reads the file through `plan.read`, which returns the planned content, and `block_update` runs first and plans a rename on every legacy path (kept, replaced, merged, kept as edited), so the hint only ever sees the current pair; no code change. Pinned by the "budget hint: a pristine legacy block" test in `tests/test-project-update.sh`.
- **(e) `install.sh` `block_size` and the line-812 routing warning** take the earliest pair of either spelling / strip only the current pair; both affect displayed text only, and `block_size` runs after `managed_block` has renamed the pair. Status: accepted.

KNOWN FACT — not the home: the test runs under `set -uo pipefail` (`:6`) and checked the 17.7 KB dry-run output with `printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q …`. Bash's `printf` writes it in 4096-byte chunks (strace: 4×4096 + 1321), the matcher line sits at byte 4258, and when `grep -q` exits on the match before `printf` has written its last chunk, `printf` dies of SIGPIPE, the pipeline returns 141 and the check fails. Measured on this machine, 3000 runs of the line-253 check: idle 0 failures; with every core busy 17 and 4 failures, all exit 141; the fixed form 0 under the same load. Fix: the 12 `printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q '…'` lines in the file became `grep -q '…' <<<"$out"` — the shell writes the here-string before grep starts, so no writer is left to receive SIGPIPE. Dropping `-q` would not help: GNU grep with stdout on `/dev/null` exits on the first match too. The same pattern elsewhere: see the next entry.

status_why: fixed for every check whose writer is a variable (2026-10-21, T1, `tests/*.sh` only). Rewritten by a script only where the writer is unquoted shell text, not in a heredoc body or a quoted string (`tests/test-fable-gate.sh:236`, the `--then` command, is left as it is); each rewritten line was checked to be the original with the writer moved into the here-string. `tests/test-install-dry-run.sh:24` now reads its `sed` span into a here-string too: with `--fable no` that span is 4339 B, so `sed` itself could take the SIGPIPE. Same input for grep: the here-string adds at most one final newline, which can only add an empty last line; no rewritten check uses `-v` or a pattern that can be empty. The 18 files before (each alone) → after (`bash tests/run-all.sh`, exit 0): the same count per file, 2188 passed, 0 failed. Found on the way, KNOWN FACT (`bash -c 'set -o pipefail; ! { echo X; sleep 0.2; echo more; } | grep -q X'` exits 0): a negative check — `! printf … | grep -q X`, or `… | grep -q X && fail || pass` — turned the race into a pass, so a real failure could go green, not only a pass red. Left as they are, about 90: command writers (`python3 "$GATE" status | grep -q`, `python3 "$UPDATE" "$P" | grep -q`, `S events … | grep -q`, `"$GUARD" | grep -q`) and `jq`/`sed`/`grep` filters between a variable and `grep -q`. Rewriting a command writer as `<<<"$(cmd)"` would drop the command's own exit status from the check under `pipefail`. Their outputs are one write: a status line, a filtered field, or a Python writer, which flushes a pipe in 8 KB blocks (measured here: `update.py` dry run 366 B, `--adopt` 2.1 KB, `state.py events --last 20 --format jsonl` 5.7 KB). A writer whose output grows past one block can still fail this way.
